recipes.name: Interdependent collaboration task graphs
recipes.summary: Build multi-agent tasks by making the work depend on itself: the collaboration requirement lives in the task dependencies and the shared resources, not in a prompt that assigns roles. Reusable collaboration structures are mined from source workflows at two levels - local patterns capturing how subtasks interact (one subtask's output feeds another's input, two subtasks contend for one resource, one must finish before another starts) and global structures describing how those interactions compose into a complete job - and recombined coarse-to-fine into new task graphs. Each graph is instantiated in an executable environment that reports partial progress as well as final resolution, so a verifier can distinguish a wrong answer from a right answer reached through broken dependencies. Roles and communication protocols are deliberately left open: which agents route work to whom is part of what is being measured.
when_to_use: the source contains workflows that decompose into subtasks with real interdependence
you need to measure collaboration itself, not only individual subtask accuracy
the environment can expose shared state that several agents read and write
not_when_to_use: the source is a single-agent task with no interaction surface
the environment cannot be run with more than one agent
inputs: a pool of source tasks or workflows that can be decomposed into subtasks
an executable environment exposing shared resources and partial progress
an explicit record of which subtask outputs feed which other subtasks

steps.title: Mine local collaboration patterns
steps.detail: Extract recurring interaction shapes between subtasks from the source workflows and store each as a structural pattern - an output-to-input edge, a resource contention, an ordering constraint - rather than as a prompt instruction.

steps.title: Mine global task structures
steps.detail: Extract the higher-level workflows that assemble those interactions into a complete job, so the bank holds both a unit of collaboration and a whole pipeline built from units, and recombination has two granularities to work with.

steps.title: Recombine coarse-to-fine
steps.detail: Compose new task graphs by substituting local patterns into global structures and instantiating the result in the environment. Vary the recombination so the new graphs mix patterns the source never combined.

steps.title: Keep dependencies, drop roles
steps.detail: Write the instruction as the end objective plus the shared resources it touches. Do not assign roles, team topologies or a communication protocol, since those choices are exactly what the task is meant to measure.

steps.title: Expose partial progress
steps.detail: The environment must report which subtasks are satisfied and which are not, so a run can be scored on how the interdependencies were handled and not only on the final artefact.

steps.title: Score two axes separately
steps.detail: Report whether the objective was reached and whether the dependencies were respected - no subtask consumed an output that had not yet been produced, no shared resource was written twice. Store both in the result so the failure is attributable.

steps.title: Run agents against one resettable world
steps.detail: Give every agent the same environment instance with isolated per-agent interfaces but shared world state, and reset that state between runs so a graph can be replayed exactly and attempts do not contaminate each other.

verifier: the final objective asserted on the shared state; test.sh writes 1 or 0 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt
dependency log check: every consumed subtask output has a producer that completed earlier in the trace
shared-resource write log contains exactly one write per resource, with no conflicting double write
the reference solution passes and the untouched workspace fails
pitfalls: pre-assigning roles lets an agent hard-code a protocol and skips the collaboration measurement
partial progress aggregated into a single number hides whether the dependencies were respected
shared state that is not reset between runs makes the second attempt trivially easier

source_papers.title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
source_papers.note: collaboration requirements embedded in task dependencies and shared-resource constraints, two-level mining of local patterns and global structures, coarse-to-fine composition, and automated verification of partial progress and complete resolution

source_papers.title: AgentSociety: Incentivizing Agentic Social Intelligence
source_papers.note: decentralised agents of heterogeneous competence route work by delegation and disclose information selectively, so the environment must support incentive-bearing communication rather than broadcast

source_papers.title: Unified Distributed Environment
source_papers.note: one virtualised interface over heterogeneous simulators, multi-agent by default, so a task graph can be executed by several agents against a single shared world

recipes.name: Mixed-motive coopetition environments with parameterised payoffs
recipes.summary: Not every multi-agent task is cooperative: real collaboration mixes conflict, so the payoff structure is declared rather than implied. Each instance belongs to a mechanism class - interdependence and complementarity, trust and reputation, collective action and loyalty, or sequential interaction and reciprocity - and carries a closed-form payoff together with a calibrated interdependence matrix that states how much each agent's outcome depends on the others. The reward layer is then parameterised over structurally distinct modes (private, integrated, cooperative), which separates payoff from reward and lets the same environment answer a cooperation test and a reward-convention ablation. Co-player behaviour is part of the design rather than an afterthought: the instance ships with a reference co-player, and where difficulty matters, the co-player policy and the environment parameters are adapted together.
when_to_use: the source describes agents with conflicting or partial interests
you want to compare how one task behaves under different reward conventions
the environment must be calibrated against a documented case rather than merely plausible
not_when_to_use: all agents share a single objective, which makes the payoff trivial
inputs: the source's interaction structure, mapped to one or more mechanism classes
a payoff specification that can be written in closed form per instance
an environment exposed through a multi-agent interface, parallel and turn-based

steps.title: Assign the mechanism class
steps.detail: Classify the instance into one of the four mechanism classes by the structure of the interaction - interdependence and complementarity, trust and reputation, collective action and loyalty, sequential interaction and reciprocity. The class fixes which parameters vary and what counts as a valid cooperative outcome.

steps.title: Declare the payoff in closed form
steps.detail: Write each agent's payoff as an explicit function of the joint outcome and derive the interdependence matrix quantifying how much each payoff moves when the others change. Keep the matrix as data in the task, not as prose.

steps.title: Parameterise the reward layer
steps.detail: Expose the reward in three structurally distinct modes - private, integrated, cooperative - over the same payoff, so the same instance can serve both a cooperation test and a reward-type ablation without editing the dynamics.

steps.title: Implement the multi-agent interfaces
steps.detail: Expose the instance through both a parallel and a turn-based interface so the same task runs under synchronous and sequential policies, and check that the underlying dynamics do not change with the interface used.

steps.title: Give the co-player a policy
steps.detail: Ship a reference co-player - a learning algorithm, a game-theoretic oracle or a heuristic - and record which one was used. A constant-action opponent makes the instance a single exploit rather than a coordination problem.

steps.title: Adapt co-player and environment together
steps.detail: Where the instance must stay hard, adapt the co-player policy and the environment parameters jointly, then check that the difficulty is not carried by a single co-player quirk that a different solver would walk around.

steps.title: Validate against a reference case
steps.detail: Where the source supplies a documented case, calibrate the instance against it and record the agreement rate as a quality metric for that instance.

verifier: the joint outcome is asserted on the environment state and per-agent payoffs are computed from the closed form and logged
switching the reward mode changes the reported reward while the trajectory stays identical
the reference co-player seeds and policy ids are stored with the task so runs are reproducible
the untouched workspace fails and writes 0 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt
pitfalls: payoff and reward conflated in one function makes ablation impossible
a fixed co-player turns the instance into an opponent exploit rather than a coordination problem
interdependence asserted qualitatively instead of supplied as a matrix cannot be calibrated

source_papers.title: Coopetition-Gym v1: A Formally Grounded Platform for Mixed-Motive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning under Strategic Coopetition
source_papers.note: closed-form payoff per instance, calibrated interdependence matrix, and a reward layer parameterised over private, integrated and cooperative modes across four mechanism classes

source_papers.title: MAESTRO: Open-Ended Environment Design for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
source_papers.note: environment parameters and co-player policies are adapted jointly, so co-player strength belongs to the difficulty budget rather than being fixed

source_papers.title: AgentSociety: Incentivizing Agentic Social Intelligence
source_papers.note: payoffs reflect marginal contribution and delegation to more competent neighbours is incentive compatible, giving the mixed-motive structure an explicit utility model
